evidence: The 2018-11-24 cyndiformayor.com capture is one hand-coded HTML page. It has no paid-for line, it sends donations to a personal 'paypal.me/Lamm4LNK' link and a dead '#' link, and it calls her 'the Republican candidate' in a nonpartisan race. Her own campaign site, cyndiforthecity.com (2018-10-15 capture), is a WordPress site with PayPal donation buttons for 'Cyndi For The City' and the footer 'Paid for by Citizens for Cyndi', and it has no link to cyndiformayor.com. The same domain carries an attack page on her by 2019-08-16, and the same server returned 403 for robots.txt from 2018-11-04 through 2020; this is consistent with one non-campaign operator from the start, though the archive does not show the registrant.

The 2014-05-20 homepage is titled 'Fraim for Mayor' and labels him 'CANDIDATE FOR MAYOR', and its footer reads 'Paid for and Authorized by Paul Fraim, Candidate for Mayor'. The 2014-05-27 feed lists posts from 2014-03-14 to 2014-05-13, including '"Friday with Fraim" set for April 11 at Campaign Headquarters' (2014-04-08). These posts show campaign activity in the weeks before the 2014-05-06 election.

Most content is from 2013: the news and endorsement items stop at 'October 17 2013'. However, the 'Byron Brown for Mayor' committee updated the site after the 2013 race. The homepage changed between 2016-01-10 and 2016-10-06, and the 2017-06-30 Events page lists 'Mayor Byron Brown's Holiday Party and Toy Drive, Thursday, December 8, 2016' under 'News on Mayor Brown's fundraising events'. The 2017-04-21 homepage, titled 'Re-Elect Mayor Byron Brown', still asks for contributions. A fundraiser 11 months before the 2017 election counts as activity for that race, but the evidence is thin: by 2017-07-12 the domain showed a default hosting page.
